questions.prompt: A company sells accounting software to other companies. Which business model is this?
questions.explanation: Business to Business (B2B): the customers are other businesses (spec 5.1.2).

questions.prompt: According to the specification, which of these is an INTERNAL stakeholder?
questions.explanation: Spec 5.1.3 lists owners, directors and employees as internal stakeholders. Shareholders are listed as external.
questions.commonMistake: Assuming shareholders are internal because they own shares.

questions.prompt: An NHS hospital is part of which sector?
questions.explanation: Public sector organisations are run by or on behalf of the government (spec 5.1.1).

questions.prompt: A charity is an example of a not-for-profit organisation.
questions.explanation: Spec 5.1.1: voluntary/charity – not for profit.

questions.prompt: Automated stock control mainly supports which organisation area?
questions.explanation: Spec 5.2.1 lists automated stock control under logistics.

questions.prompt: Match each organisation area to a way digital systems support it.
pairs: Real-time monitoring of key performance indicators
Better financial reporting from up-to-date information
questions.explanation: All examples are taken from spec 5.2.1.

questions.prompt: A booking website shows 'Your request is being processed – this may take up to 30 seconds'. Which way of meeting user needs does this show?
options: Reduction of pain points through communicating expected response time
questions.explanation: Spec 5.2.2: reducing pain points includes communicating the expected response time.

questions.prompt: A ransomware attack stops staff opening customer records. Which part of a security breach does this mainly show?
questions.explanation: The data still exists but cannot be accessed, so availability is reduced (spec 5.3.1).

questions.prompt: Which is a potential IMPACT on an organisation of a risk such as a data breach?
questions.explanation: Spec 5.3.2 impacts: legal action, fines, reputational damage, withdrawal of licence to practise, loss of business. The other options are risks, not impacts.

questions.prompt: Match each method of implementing change to its description.
pairs: Old and new systems run at the same time until the new one is proven
The new system is introduced one part at a time
The old system is switched off and the new one starts immediately
The new system is trialled in one department or site first
questions.explanation: Spec 5.4.4 lists parallel, phased, direct and pilot.
questions.commonMistake: Confusing phased (part of the system at a time) with pilot (part of the organisation first).

questions.prompt: A hospital cannot risk losing patient records if a new system fails, and has enough staff to enter data twice for a short time. Which implementation method is most suitable?
questions.explanation: Parallel running keeps the old system working as a fallback, which suits high-risk data, at the cost of extra work.

questions.prompt: What is a role of a change advisory board (CAB)?
options: To review and prioritise change requests
To write the code for every change
questions.explanation: Spec 5.4.4: the CAB prioritises and reviews change requests, manages stages of approval, monitors change and gives feedback.

questions.prompt: SMARTER objectives are specific, measurable, achievable, realistic, time-bound, evaluated and ___.
questions.explanation: Spec 5.4.4 defines SMARTER as specific, measurable, achievable, realistic, time-bound, evaluated, reviewed.

questions.prompt: Which of these is an EXTERNAL factor that could trigger change in an organisation?
options: A zero-day vulnerability in software the company uses
questions.explanation: Zero-day vulnerabilities are a technological external factor (spec 5.4.2). The others are internal factors (5.4.1).

questions.prompt: Why is rollback planning important when changing a system?
options: So the organisation can return to a working state if the change fails
So the change can be made faster
So staff do not need training
questions.explanation: Spec 5.4.4: rollback planning covers backup methodology, backup location and recovery plan.

questions.prompt: A small airline plans to replace paper maintenance records with a new digital system. Evaluate the feasibility of this project.
markPoints: Benefits: productivity gains, faster access to records, improved communication
Costs of implementing the change, including hardware, software and training
Risks such as resistance to change from the workforce or inadequate knowledge of the new system
Disruption caused while the new system is implemented
Constraints of budget, time, and human and technological resources
A supported conclusion about whether the project is feasible
questions.explanation: Spec 5.4.5 feasibility factors: benefits and drawbacks, risks and constraints. 'Evaluate' requires a judgement.

questions.prompt: The value '38.5' with no context is best described as:
questions.explanation: Data is raw values without context. '38.5°C, patient temperature' is information; knowing that this means the patient has a fever is knowledge.

questions.prompt: Match each term to an example.
pairs: A temperature of 38.5°C means the patient has a fever and needs treatment
questions.explanation: Spec 6.1.1: data gains context to become information; information applied with understanding becomes knowledge.

questions.prompt: Why can AI/machine learning be a risky source for generating data?
options: A feedback loop can reinforce errors or bias when outputs are used as new training data
questions.explanation: Spec 6.1.2 highlights the dangers of the feedback loop in AI/machine learning data.

questions.prompt: Which is a metric used to determine the value of data?
questions.explanation: Spec 6.1.3: quantity, timeframe, source and veracity.

questions.prompt: Written comments in a customer feedback form are:
questions.explanation: Free text is qualitative and unstructured (spec 6.3.3).

questions.prompt: Match each piece of data to how quantitative data is represented.
pairs: Number of passengers on a flight
Seat class: economy, business or first
questions.explanation: Discrete values are counted; continuous values are measured; categorical values fall into groups (spec 6.3.4).

questions.prompt: Which data type is most suitable for storing a scanned image in a database?
questions.explanation: A Blob (binary large object) stores binary data such as images or audio (spec 6.4.1).

questions.prompt: Which data type holds a single letter such as 'Y'?
questions.explanation: A character stores a single symbol.

questions.prompt: Match each data format to its description.
pairs: Plain text with values separated by commas, one record per line
Key–value pairs and arrays, often used by web APIs
Data wrapped in custom opening and closing tags
A variable-length Unicode encoding for characters from all languages
questions.explanation: Spec 6.5.1 data formats.

questions.prompt: A web app must store user names containing characters such as é and 中. Which encoding should it use?
questions.explanation: ASCII only has 128 characters. UTF-8 can represent characters from every language.

questions.prompt: Which is an example of metadata for a photo?
options: The date and time the photo was taken
questions.explanation: Metadata is data that describes other data, giving context (spec 6.6.1).

questions.prompt: Match each V of Big Data to its meaning.
pairs: The speed at which data is generated and processed
The different types and formats of data
How accurate and trustworthy the data is
How the meaning or structure of data changes over time
How useful the data is to the organisation
questions.explanation: Spec 6.7.1 lists the six Vs.
questions.commonMistake: Confusing variety (different types) with variability (changes over time).

questions.prompt: Asking a user to type their new email address twice is an example of:
questions.explanation: Double entry is verification: it checks the data was entered accurately (spec 6.8.5).

questions.prompt: Typing the year 1945 as 1954 is an example of:
questions.explanation: A transposition error swaps characters around. A transcription error is copying something incorrectly, e.g. mishearing or misreading.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of data wrangling in order.
questions.explanation: Spec 6.8.2 lists the data wrangling steps: structure, clean, validate, enrich, output.

questions.prompt: Which method reduces data entry errors by only allowing the user to pick from fixed choices?
questions.explanation: Drop-down menus prevent spelling and transcription errors (spec 6.8.5).

questions.prompt: Which visualisation is best for showing how daily passenger numbers changed over 30 days?
questions.explanation: A line graph shows trends over time. A pie chart shows parts of a whole at one moment.

questions.prompt: Which data model organises data as a tree in which each child record has only one parent?
questions.explanation: In a hierarchical model each child has one parent. A network model allows records to have many parents (spec 6.10.1).

questions.prompt: Which data model stores data in tables of rows and columns linked by keys?
questions.explanation: Spec 6.10.4: relational models are drawn with tables, rows, columns and labels.

questions.prompt: In role-based access control (RBAC), permissions are given based on:
questions.explanation: RBAC grants access rights by role, e.g. all engineers can edit maintenance records.

questions.prompt: Explain one benefit of an airline giving a partner travel company access to flight data through an API rather than direct database access.
markPoints: Only the data the partner needs is exposed
The partner never connects directly to the database, reducing security risk
Access can be controlled, monitored or revoked using API keys
Data is returned in a standard format (e.g. JSON), making integration easier
questions.explanation: Spec 6.11.1–6.11.2 benefits and drawbacks of access mechanisms.

questions.prompt: Which stores very large amounts of raw data in its original format until it is needed?
questions.explanation: A data lake holds raw data. A data warehouse holds processed, structured data; a data mart is a subset for one department.

questions.prompt: Which processor feature allows more tasks to be processed at the same time?
questions.explanation: Each core can process instructions, so more cores allow more tasks to run simultaneously (spec 7.1.2).

questions.prompt: Which type of memory loses its contents when power is turned off?
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile; ROM is not.

questions.prompt: Which type of secondary storage has no moving parts?
questions.explanation: Solid state storage uses flash memory with no moving parts.

questions.prompt: A cash machine must respond to each transaction immediately. Which type of operating system is most suitable?
questions.explanation: Spec 7.2.1 lists transaction processing and monitoring/control as uses of real-time operating systems.

questions.prompt: Which operating system feature gives each running task a short turn on the processor?
questions.explanation: Multitasking operating systems use time-slicing and interrupts (spec 7.2.1).

questions.prompt: Which translator converts and runs source code one line at a time?
questions.explanation: An interpreter translates and executes line by line; a compiler translates the whole program first (spec 7.2.3).

questions.prompt: Which utility rearranges the parts of files on a magnetic hard disk so they are stored together?
questions.explanation: Spec 7.2.2 common utilities.

questions.prompt: Bluetooth headphones connected to a phone form a:
questions.explanation: A personal area network covers a few metres around one person.

questions.prompt: In which topology is every device connected to one central switch?
questions.explanation: Spec 7.3.4 topologies: star, mesh, tree.

questions.prompt: Put the seven layers of the OSI model in order from layer 7 (top) to layer 1 (bottom).
questions.explanation: Spec 7.3.7. One way to remember from the top: All People Seem To Need Data Processing.

questions.prompt: Put the four layers of the TCP/IP model in order from top to bottom, using the specification's names.
questions.explanation: Spec 7.3.8 names the layers application, transport, internet and network. Other sources call the bottom layer network access or link.

questions.prompt: Match each protocol to its role.
pairs: Accessing email that stays stored on the server
Automatically assigning IP addresses to devices
Translating domain names into IP addresses
questions.explanation: Spec 7.3.10 common network protocols.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a routing protocol?
questions.explanation: RIP and OSPF are routing protocols (spec 7.3.10).

questions.prompt: What is a cyclic redundancy check (CRC) used for in data packets?
questions.explanation: The sender calculates a CRC value; the receiver recalculates it and a mismatch shows the data was corrupted (spec 7.3.9).

questions.prompt: What is latency?
options: The maximum amount of data that can be sent per second
The number of devices on a network
questions.explanation: Bandwidth is capacity; latency is delay (spec 7.3.11).

questions.prompt: In which network model do all computers have equal status and share resources directly with each other?
questions.explanation: Spec 7.3.5 network models.

questions.prompt: What is a type 1 hypervisor?
options: One that runs directly on the physical hardware
One that runs as an application on a host operating system
questions.explanation: Type 1 (bare-metal) runs directly on hardware; type 2 runs on top of a host operating system (spec 7.4.1).

questions.prompt: Which is a drawback of virtual environments listed in the specification?
questions.explanation: Spec 7.4.4 drawbacks: extra hardware load, slower execution, potential false representation of performance.

questions.prompt: Match each cloud delivery model to what the CLIENT manages.
pairs: Application software, data and user accounts
Application software, operating system, runtime, data and user accounts
questions.explanation: Spec 7.5.3 sets out responsibility for each model.

questions.prompt: Which cloud benefit means resources can be increased or decreased quickly to match demand?
questions.explanation: Spec 7.5.2 benefits of cloud.

questions.prompt: An airline must choose between buying a physical server or renting a cloud server with support for a new maintenance system. Evaluate the two options.
markPoints: Cloud: no large upfront hardware cost and elasticity to match demand
Cloud with support: provider manages hardware, so no in-house technician is needed
Cloud: depends on internet connectivity and has ongoing monthly costs that add up over years
Physical: organisation controls the hardware and data location but must maintain it and replace it
Considers security or legal compliance of where data is stored
questions.explanation: 'Evaluate' needs both sides and a justified judgement in context.

questions.prompt: Which backup site has equipment and up-to-date data ready to take over almost immediately?
questions.explanation: A hot site is ready at once; a warm site needs some setup; a cold site is only space and power (spec 7.6.2).

questions.prompt: What is device hardening?
options: Removing unneeded ports, applications, permissions and access
questions.explanation: Spec 7.6.2 device hardening.

questions.prompt: Which is classed as access information?
questions.explanation: Spec 8.1.1 access information: usernames, passwords, MFA details, PINs, access codes, passphrases, biometric data.

questions.prompt: Why should an organisation keep its client details confidential?
options: To prevent competitors contacting its clients and to protect client privacy
questions.explanation: Spec 8.1.2.

questions.prompt: Match each social engineering attack to its description.
pairs: Fraudulent emails sent to large numbers of people
A fraudulent message targeted at a specific person or organisation
Redirecting users from a genuine website to a fake one
questions.explanation: Spec 8.2.1 social engineering.

questions.prompt: Typing ' OR '1'='1 into a website login box is an attempt at:
questions.explanation: The input tries to change the database query so the condition is always true.

questions.prompt: A website is flooded with requests from thousands of infected computers so real users cannot access it. What is this?
questions.explanation: A distributed denial of service attack often uses a botnet (spec 8.2.1).

questions.prompt: Which malware encrypts files and demands payment to unlock them?
questions.explanation: Spec 8.2.1 malware types.

questions.prompt: How should an organisation respond to a malicious employee, according to the specification?
options: Give them a warning and continue as normal
questions.explanation: Spec 8.2.3: immediate removal from premises and suspending user accounts immediately.

questions.prompt: Someone follows an employee through a secure door without using their own pass. What is this?
questions.explanation: Spec 8.2.4: do not allow tailgating.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of hashing a password before storing it?
options: So the original password is not stored and cannot simply be read if the database is stolen
So the password can be decrypted later when the user forgets it
questions.explanation: Hashing is one-way. The system hashes the login attempt and compares hashes, so the plain password never needs to be stored.
questions.commonMistake: Thinking hashing is the same as encryption and can be reversed.

questions.prompt: Which type of encryption uses a public key to encrypt and a private key to decrypt?
questions.explanation: Spec 8.3.1: hashing, symmetric and asymmetric encryption.

questions.prompt: Which backup type copies only the data changed since the last FULL backup?
questions.explanation: Differential backups copy changes since the last full backup. Incremental backups copy changes since the last backup of any type.

questions.prompt: Which of these is multi-factor authentication?
options: A password plus a code sent to a registered phone
questions.explanation: MFA combines different kinds of factor, e.g. something you know and something you have. A password and a PIN are both things you know.

questions.prompt: An air gap physically isolates a computer or network from unsecured networks such as the internet.
questions.explanation: Spec 8.3.1 threat mitigation techniques include air gaps.

questions.prompt: What is penetration testing?
options: Authorised simulated attacks to find vulnerabilities before criminals do
Testing how many users a website can handle
questions.explanation: Spec 8.3.1 penetration testing includes ethical hacking.

questions.prompt: Explain why staff training helps reduce the risk of social engineering attacks.
markPoints: Staff learn to recognise signs of attacks such as phishing emails or suspicious calls
Staff are less likely to reveal passwords or click malicious links
Staff know how to report suspected attacks quickly
questions.explanation: Social engineering targets people, not technology, so training reduces human error.

questions.prompt: Which part of the CIA triad ensures data has not been tampered with?
questions.explanation: Spec 8.4.1.

questions.prompt: Match each stage of the IAAA model to an example.
pairs: Only allowing access to permitted resources
Audit logs tracing actions back to a user
questions.explanation: Spec 8.4.2 IAAA model.
questions.commonMistake: Confusing authentication (proving who you are) with authorisation (what you may do).
